dernierCall.guidanceProchainTrimestre: No quarterly guidance (semi-annual reporter). For H2 26 management explicitly guides to lower percentage growth on tough comparables while absolute sales keep rising above H1: Advanced Synthesis growth and margins normalize (margins around 40% vs 48.1% in H1, the 2025-into-2026 phasing benefit does not repeat), Integrated Biologics absorbs the extended Vacaville CDMO-readiness shutdown partly offset by the Visp 6x20,000L large-scale mammalian start-up, and Specialized Modalities gets a larger Cell & Gene contribution after the return to normal operations late in H1.
dernierCall.guidanceAnnuelle: FY26 outlook UPGRADED at the H1 call: CORE EBITDA margin raised to 33-34% (from '>32%'; the CFO explicitly frames 33% as the annual floor), CER sales growth reconfirmed at 11-12% (implies ~6-8% in H2 against a high prior-year base). FX headwind of -2 to -3pp expected on FY reported sales (concentrated in H1, USD-driven). Capex to remain mid-to-high teens as % of sales with some phasing into 2027; >CHF 7bn organic capex through 2030 under strict return criteria (IRR >=15%, ROIC at peak >=30%). Mid-term algorithm unchanged: low-teens CER sales growth on average over time with continuously expanding margins and cash generation. Capital Markets Day in Vacaville in October 2026.
pointsCles: Broad-based beat-quality half: all three platforms grew double-digit CER - Integrated Biologics +10.0% (CHF 1.87bn sales, margin flat at a solid 36.0%), Advanced Synthesis +27.7% (CHF 834m, CORE EBITDA margin 48.1%, +6.8pp, driven by Small Molecules and especially Bioconjugates off a low base; underlying growth low teens), Specialized Modalities +22.6% (CHF 553m, margin 28.0%, +10.7pp on the Microbial rebound and Bioscience; margins now approaching group average). Group: sales CHF 3.4bn +16% CER (+11.2% reported, ~5pp FX headwind), CORE EBITDA CHF 1.2bn (+27.4%), margin 34.8% (+4.4pp), FCF CHF 426m (vs 116m), capex CHF 530m (15.7% of sales vs 21.2%), annualized ROIC 13.2% (~2x WACC per CFO).

Pure-play CDMO transformation COMPLETED in under 15 months: agreement signed to divest Capsules & Health Ingredients to Lone Star (EV CHF 2.3bn, closing before year-end 2026; CHI now in discontinued operations, H1 25 restated and republished 23 June 2026). CHF 500m of surplus capital earmarked for an accelerated buyback at closing, the balance to deleveraging - the group swings to net cash into 2027.

Growth pipeline strengthened: long-term strategic collaboration extended with a leading US biopharma spanning all US commercial sites; sixth commercial cell & gene therapy approved in the network; two new ADC investments announced (highly potent payload-linker suites in Visp, ramp-up from 2029; second commercial aseptic ADC filling line in Stein, ramp-up from 2030 with a big-pharma anchor customer, peak sales by mid-2030s); Stein large-scale fill-finish scope broadened to high-value small-molecule drug products (small extra capex, start pushed to 2028); Visp 6x20,000L mammalian asset begins operations in H2 26; Vacaville CDMO-readiness on track (five contracts already offset the Roche run-off through 2028, growth contribution after 2028, FY26 site sales ~CHF 0.6bn flat).

H2 deliberately framed as normalization, not deterioration: tougher comps and less favorable phasing (mainly Advanced Synthesis), Vacaville extended shutdown a known drag; FY margin floor 33%. Demand backdrop intact - management sees no change in big-pharma outsourcing behavior, US capacity demand particularly high (Portsmouth, Vacaville), large-pharma capex/sales stable at ~5% through 2030, customer mix balanced (~45% of revenue with small/mid biotech). Market nonetheless marked the stock down ~6% on the unchanged revenue guidance.

hypothese.text:
== THESIS SUMMARY ==
World-leading pharma/biotech CDMO (Integrated Biologics, Advanced Synthesis, Specialized Modalities) riding structural outsourcing growth. H1 26: CORE EBITDA margin guidance RAISED to 33-34% (from >32%) on biologics mix, CER growth held at 11-12% despite a -2/-3% FX headwind on reported sales. The CHI divestment (2.3bn CHF net proceeds; closing end-2026) reshapes the balance sheet: 500M to an accelerated buyback, 1.8bn to deleveraging - net cash through 2026-2027.

== THESIS READ ==
- The margin raise is mix-quality evidence (biologics utilization), not a one-off. Watch: Integrated Biologics order intake and 2027 capacity ramp (Vacaville).
- The 2027 EPS dip (16.34 vs 18.47) is the CHI-exit earnings hole before the redeployment compounds - optics, not deterioration. Watch: closing accounts to size the hole precisely.
- Buyback (500M accelerated) plus net-cash position gives allocation optionality rare in the CDMO space. Watch: bolt-on M&A vs further buybacks.

== SPECIAL FACTORS ==
Base = IFRS as reported (CORE gap ~2% only this semester, not retreated per user instruction - only true exceptionals). Any CHI disposal GAIN will be excluded as a pure one-off at booking. BRIDGE CAVEAT (flagged): the projected 'other' line is a fitted below-EBIT block (CHI-exit effects, stranded costs, financing swings) - LOW CONFIDENCE, to rebuild at the CHI closing. priorEPS null (young fiche).

== PARAMETERS & WATCH-LIST ==
2026: revenue 7,118M CHF, EBIT 1,601M, EPS 18.47 (includes CHI stub); 2027-2030: ~9-10%/yr CER ex-CHI, margin drift, shares -1.4%/yr (buyback). ETR 20%. Watch: CHI closing accounts (bridge rebuild trigger); FX; biologics pricing environment.

== CATALYSTS ==
CHI closing (end-2026) + accelerated buyback execution; FY26 results (late Jan 2027); Vacaville/capacity utilization milestones; CDMO demand prints from big-pharma outsourcing.

ancrages.moteur: FY2026 guidance raised for the second consecutive time in Q2 26: CORE EBITDA margin 33-34% (from >32%), CER growth confirmed at 11-12% - strong operational execution across the three Business Platforms, all at double-digit CER growth in H1.

Disposal of Capsules & Health Ingredients (CHI) to Lone Star Funds for 2,3 Md CHF, closing expected before end-2026 - CHI still contributes to 2026 earnings (until closing) but is entirely excluded from the 2027+ projections, creating a deliberate scope discontinuity in the model. Disposal gain expected but not quantified, treated as a genuine one-off excluded from omniumNet.

500 M CHF of excess capital to be returned through an accelerated buyback programme as soon as the CHI disposal closes, on top of the buyback programme already running since 2023 - gradual reduction in the share count over the projection horizon.

Organic investment plan of more than 7 Md CHF out to 2030 (ADC expansions at Stein and Visp, mammalian, drug product, bioconjugate, cell & gene capacity) - CapEx intensity targeted in the middle of the mid-to-high-teens range as a % of sales for 2026, with normalisation and 2026-2027 phasing; supports the 2027-2030 revenue/EBIT growth trajectory but keeps pressure on deleveraging.

Management explicitly indicates that H2 26 growth and margin will be more normalised than H1 (phasing favourable to H1 at Advanced Synthesis in particular, higher 2025 comparison base in H2) - modelled as a sequential deceleration in organic growth over the second half of the year, without calling the overall annual guidance into question.

Net proceeds from the CHI disposal (2,3 Md CHF) allocated consistently: 500 M CHF to the accelerated buyback (see AN-BUYBACK-500M), the remaining 1,8 Md CHF applied to deleveraging at closing (expected end-2026). The group thus moves into a net cash position at end-2026 and end-2027 (negative omniumND), which implies near-zero net financial charges or even a slight net financial income over those two years (instead of the usual interest charge on positive net debt) - omniumNet 2026-2027 revised up accordingly relative to a calculation that would have frozen the pre-disposal EBIT-to-net conversion ratio. The gradual return of net debt into positive territory from 2029-2030 (funding of the CapEx plan >7 Md CHF out to 2030) restores a modest but not negligible net financial charge.

2025.residualNote: Below-EBIT block ~-364M at 20% tax: financing plus non-operating items (restructuring/impairment residuals). NOTE: across the projected years the 'other' line is a FITTED below-EBIT block (CHI-perimeter exit effects, stranded costs, financing swings around the 2.3bn CHF disposal proceeds) - LOW CONFIDENCE by construction, to rebuild line-by-line at the CHI closing (end-2026) when the disposal accounting is published. 2026: finNet -40 = interest on the intra-year average debt (the 1.8bn deleveraging lands only at the CHI closing, end-2026); the +102 'other' belongs to the same fitted CHI-transition block.
